record.category: discovery layer over the public Mainline DHT, published from an iroh node the user runs

free_tier.stated: No quota, no storage. Pure discovery: publishes BLAKE3->provider mappings onto the public BitTorrent Mainline DHT.

egress.terms: UDP DHT traffic only, kilobytes. Mainline lookups measured at 37 ms in n0's own example.

record.tooling: Publishes a signed endpoint record (endpoint id + UDP socket + timestamp) to a tiny UDP address-index service, then `announce_peer` for SHA-1(BLAKE3 hash). Discovery returns candidate EndpointIds which are then dialled with normal iroh hole punching.
record.chaining: Removes the last central dependency: no DNS, no pkarr relay, no account. Requires at least one reachable address-index service, found by rendezvous hash or a curated BEP 44 record.
record.limits_note: Mainline traffic is unencrypted and 'easily blocked by middleboxes'; no privacy ('anybody can look up your ip address'); the address-index service is last-writer-wins, in-memory, and records expire. Publishers must re-announce on a schedule.
record.reliability_note: Experimental repo (12 stars, last push 2026-10-16). SHA-1 is used only as a keyspace key, so a malicious DHT answer can waste time but cannot corrupt data. Verification is against the BLAKE3 root.

evidence.proved: announce/discovery workflow, udp-addr-index rationale, 37 ms lookup, 'mainline does not provide any privacy'
